incident: Hide Your RDP: Password Spray Leads to RansomHub Deployment (TTR ~118h)

sources.title: Hide Your RDP: Password Spray Leads to RansomHub Deployment - The DFIR Report (2025-06-30)
sources.what_it_gave: entry (password spray on internet-facing RDP), hops (RDP beachhead->2 DCs, then backup servers, file servers, hypervisors, more DCs), cred access (Mimikatz, Nirsoft CredentialsFileView, LSASS), exfil (Rclone SFTP over 443), impact (RansomHub amd64.exe local + SMB spread via remote service), TTR ~118h / 6 days

narrative_before: In a November 2024 intrusion the DFIR Report observed a password-spray attack against an internet-facing RDP server. Hours later the actor logged in over RDP with a compromised user, ran net discovery and used Mimikatz and Nirsoft CredentialsFileView against LSASS. ~2 hours after authenticating they moved by RDP to two domain controllers, examined DNS via the GUI, and continued to other servers and endpoints harvesting credentials; Advanced IP Scanner was downloaded and run from the beachhead. They continued lateral movement to backup servers, file servers, hypervisors and more domain controllers, running Mimikatz and viewing file-share documents. On day 2 they re-ran Advanced IP Scanner and SoftPerfect NetScan and installed Atera on two backup servers. On day 3 Rclone exfiltrated files over SFTP (port 443). On day 5 they returned via Splashtop on a backup server, swept the network, RDPed to hosts including domain controllers and reset user passwords. On day 6 they dropped amd64.exe (RansomHub) and ran it with a pass flag: it encrypted locally and spread over SMB, executing on remote hosts via a random-named remote service, killing VMs, deleting shadow copies and clearing logs. TTR was ~118 hours over six days.

detection_moments.description: Password spray against an internet-facing RDP server; login with a compromised user; net discovery; Mimikatz/CredentialsFileView against LSASS.
detection_moments.evidence: 'a password spray attack targeting an internet-facing RDP server ... Credential access tools, specifically Mimikatz and Nirsoft CredentialsFileView, were used' - Hide Your RDP, The DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: ~2h: RDP to two DCs, then backup servers, file servers, hypervisors and more DCs with a privileged account; Mimikatz across hosts; shares viewed; Advanced IP Scanner/NetScan.
detection_moments.evidence: 'used RDP to move laterally to two domain controllers ... continued lateral movement to additional hosts targeting backup servers, file servers, hypervisors, and more domain controllers' - Hide Your RDP

detection_moments.description: Day 3: Rclone exfiltrates documents/spreadsheets/emails/images over SFTP (port 443); Atera/Splashtop persistence on backup servers.
detection_moments.evidence: 'they employed Rclone to exfiltrate files over SFTP ... configured to include specific file types ... The transfer occurred over port 443, but the traffic was confirmed to be SFTP' - Hide Your RDP

detection_moments.description: Day 6 (~118h): amd64.exe (RansomHub) run with a pass flag; encrypts locally and spreads over SMB, executing on remote hosts via a random-named remote service; kills VMs, deletes shadow copies, clears logs.
detection_moments.evidence: 'dropped the binary named amd64.exe and executed it ... reached out to remote hosts to transfer a copy of the ransomware over SMB and then execute that file on the hosts using a remote service' - Hide Your RDP

attack_path: password spray against an internet-facing RDP server (T1110.003/T1133)
RDP to a domain controller ~2h after entry (T1021.001)
RDP lateral movement to hypervisors, file and backup servers (T1021.001)
RDP to file server; Rclone SFTP exfiltration over 443 (T1021.001/T1567.002)
RansomHub amd64.exe spreads over SMB and runs via a remote service (T1486/T1021.002)
ambiguities: Hosts named by role only; victim sector not stated. Multiple hosts of each role collapsed to one representative each (plus two DCs the report names).
Remote-encrypted hosts via SMB spread modelled as srv_1/pc_1.
Moments are the report's own daily timeline markers, not a defender detection timeline.
